## What changed

**The champion improved this task, and the run recorded it as a regression.** cap-evolve's `RESULT`
line names it in the `broke={}` set:

> ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.962 Δ=+0.086 · fixed={…} · broke={bench-aap2-006-log-root-cause,
> **bench-aap2-008-preceding-task**}

Measured inside the same iteration at the same trial count:

- the seed, re-measured at `n=9`, scored **0.844**
- `cand_0001`, at `n=9`, scored **0.978**

That is **+0.133 — an improvement**, on a task the run reports as broken with a Δ of `−0.022`. The
`−0.022` is measured against a *reused* `n=3` `seed` value of `1.000` (`[1.000, 1.000, 1.000]`) that
was never re-measured. Three ceiling trials drawn from a distribution whose `n=9` mode is `0.800`.

This task has **no errored trials in either cell**, so the sign flip is not a denominator question. It
is purely `n=3` against `n=9`. Together with [`006`](v2-bench-aap2-006-log-root-cause.md), which is
exactly flat at `n=9`, **both entries in this run's `broke={}` list are wrong.**

## What worked

**The ordering discrimination — on every trial, for both artifacts.** With weights `0.2 / 0.8`, one
expected call and two required facts, the values resolve uniquely:

| observed | expected calls matched | answer facts | seed @ n=9 | `cand_0001` @ n=9 |
|--:|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| 0.800 | **0 of 1** | 2 of 2 | 7 | 1 |
| 1.000 | 1 of 1 | 2 of 2 | 2 | **8** |

The answer component was **2 of 2 on all 18 trials**. The agent always identified both the failing
task (`Start broker service`, counter 5) and the task immediately preceding it (`Install broker
package 4.2.1`, counter 4). The entire spread is the tool call, and the champion moved it from 2-of-9
to 8-of-9.

That is worth stating plainly because this scenario was built to test ordering, and the ordering was
never in doubt. The provenance predicted the failure mode in arithmetic:

> An agent that correctly finds the failed event but reads the preceding task as the first task in the
> play now scores 0.6 instead of 0.733… However, 0.6 should not be read as "mostly succeeded."

**`0.600` never appears in this task's data.** Not once, in any run, for any artifact. The four
surrounding distractor task names — counter 2 `Stop broker service`, counter 3 `Back up broker data
directory`, counter 6 `Verify broker health endpoint` — were never taken. The discrimination axis is
sound and the skill clears it.

## What didn't

**The `0.800` mode is a missing `get_job_events` call, on a task whose author called that call
obvious.** The weight rationale reads: *"`tool_calls: 0.2` because `get_job_events` is a single,
obvious call that a lazy agent makes anyway."* On 7 of the seed's 9 trials it did not make it — and
still answered both facts correctly, presumably from `get_job_log` output. The 0.2 weight was set on
the assumption that the call was free; measured, it is the only thing this task discriminated on.

**Which champion edit fixed it is not recorded.** The plausible candidate is the Rule 4 rewrite that
stopped treating a second call on the same job as a redundant re-fetch, or the Investigation Flow
step-4 rewrite that names `get_job_events` explicitly for failed jobs. But the iteration-2 optimizer
**wrote no handover at all** — `## Iteration cand_0001 — (no handover written by the optimizer)` — so
the run contains no statement of intent to check against. Six edits shipped together and the per-task
attribution is inference from the reward decomposition, not from the record.

**And the sign error propagated into the run's own conclusions.** A `broke={}` entry is the signal a
subsequent iteration is instructed to act on: *"an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with
`broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign."* Had iteration 3 run, it would have
been told to redesign an edit that produced a `+0.133` gain here. (Iteration 3 did start and was
aborted — see `results/v2/runs/run_run_20260818_161550/`, role `discarded-aborted-iter3`.)

## What we can (or can't) learn

**The methodological finding is the one that generalises: `--reuse-baseline` across a change in
`num_trials` invalidates every per-task verdict in the run.** This task is the cleanest demonstration
because the sign actually flips: `−0.022` reported, `+0.133` measured. The fix is mechanical — re-measure
the seed at the iteration's own `n`, which this run in fact *did* (`seed_train` at `n=9` exists and is
committed) and then did not gate against. The number was collected and ignored.

**We can also learn that this scenario's pre-run design review paid off.** Dropping the `cause`
required fact was justified as an *encoding* fix, not a difficulty change:

> `failing-task` and `cause` both derive from the same `runner_on_failed` event at counter 5 — finding
> that event yields both facts. This made the first half of the question worth 2/3 of the answer
> component, while the ordering half (the scenario's actual purpose) was worth only 1/3.

With two facts instead of three, each sub-question carries half the answer weight. And the measured
result is that both halves were always satisfied — so the rebalance never had to do its work here, but
the task's remaining signal (the tool call) is uncontaminated by it.

**We cannot say the champion is at ceiling.** One trial in nine still loses the call. And this task's
`+0.133` is the third-largest equal-`n` gain in the run while being reported as a regression, which is
the most concise statement of what is wrong with this run's measurement design.
